investigations.name: bimolecular-hybrid
investigations.title: A_particle + B_field → C_field: two-way nonlinear coupling, both solvers
investigations.objective:
When particles consume a field (B substantially depleted by A), do the co-simulation
and the native VCell hybrid agree with each other and with the deterministic continuum
limit?

investigations.name: cosim-boundary-transfer
investigations.description:
Infrastructure (feature PR #21):
- the particle_positions store;
- FenicsxMeshReactionDiffusion(particle_transfer="positions"), the exact P1 load Σ_p φ_j(x_p);
- mesh.PointLocator, the voxel → tet lookup;
- mesh.boundary_triangles, with the Smoldyn "triangles" geometry (membrane="mesh").

Found while running this study: a Smoldyn-fork bug in field-dependent 0th-order creation
inside a compartment (virtualcell/Smoldyn pyhybrid a773562).
- zeroreact drew Poisson(rate·dt·cell) only in cells whose **centre** is inside the
  compartment, then discarded molecules placed outside it.
- Cells that partly overlap a curved compartment with their centre outside never created.
- Monte Carlo on this geometry: creation was 0.976 of the compartment volume. That is the
  0.974 creation deficit measured in B2b.
- The fix: every cell draws, and the existing thinning makes the count exactly
  Poisson(rate·dt·|cell ∩ compartment|).
- tests/test_smoldyn_hybrid.py::test_zeroth_order_creation_matches_curved_compartment_area
  fails without the fix (−7.8%) and passes with it.
- vcell-fvsolver's vendored Smoldyn has the same centre test. It plausibly accounts for
  the native 0.960 creation in B2b. Filed as virtualcell/vcell-fvsolver#26.
investigations.title: Removing the co-simulation's boundary artifact: particle transfer, membrane geometry and curved-compartment creation
investigations.objective:
B2c found the co-simulation's ensemble-mean B 1.3% too high in the outer shell of the ball.
Two causes were candidates:
- the two-stage particle transfer (nearest grid node, then Pᵀ to mesh DOFs);
- the domain mismatch: Smoldyn's exact sphere holds about 1.4% more volume than the
  inscribed P1 mesh.
Which is it, and what does removing it cost?

investigations.name: coupled-sparks-fast-diffusion
investigations.description:
The native solver is driven as in C1 (VCell math generation, channels placed at their
nodes, VCell's no-op O → O process dropped). One fix found here also applies to C1:
VCell mass action with no reactants drops Kf, so the constant leak V_p·U₀ vanished
from the native PDE. Before that fix the native solver was biased (mean |z| = 11.5);
it is now written as General kinetics.
Deviations (provisional) as in C1: Δz = 0.25; channel coordinates are author-approved
defaults.
investigations.title: Schaff et al. 2016, Test 2 / Fig 2: coupled calcium sparks in the fast-diffusion limit, both solvers
investigations.objective:
With channel opening coupled to local calcium (k_on·U(rᵢ)/U₀) and fast diffusion
(D = 1000 µm²/s), do both hybrid solvers reproduce the distributions of calcium and
open-channel number given by the exact well-mixed process, as in Fig 2 of the paper?

investigations.name: coupling-interval-convergence
investigations.title: Coupling error vs Smoldyn step multiplier, co-simulation (two schemes) and native VCell
investigations.objective:
How does the error of the lagged explicit coupling grow with the coupling interval
k·Δt (Smoldyn steps once per k PDE steps)? Does the co-simulation reproduce
fvsolver's coupling error, and does process-bigraph's plain scheduling
("start-of-interval") do better or worse?

investigations.name: dumbbell-three-ways
investigations.description:
Shows that one description drives every path: `to_vcml_geometry` for the native solver,
`VCellFVRealization` for the co-sim on VCell's geometry, and `realize_fenics` (Netgen) for the
mesh path. The native runners now pass `geometry`, `region` and `domain_volume` through
(`run_native`, `run_native_ensemble`).

Each method's B is measured on its own PDE volumes. The membrane distance is taken from the
Netgen surface, the closest to the analytic shape.
investigations.title: One non-convex GeometryDescription, three solver paths: native VCell, co-sim on VCell's geometry, co-sim on a Netgen mesh
investigations.objective:
Phase 7e end to end on a non-sphere: does one geometry description drive the native VCell solver
and both co-simulation paths, and do the accessible-volume correction and the body-fitted mesh
stay unbiased and conservative on a thin-necked, non-convex shape?

investigations.name: fenicsx-same-problem
investigations.description:
The swap is one composite argument (build_hybrid_document(pde_engine="fenicsx")); the
SmoldynHybrid process, the coupling and the model are untouched. In VCell the PDE
discretization is part of the solver (vcell-fvsolver's FV scheme, or vcell-fenics as a
separate solver), rather than an interchangeable component of the hybrid coupling.
investigations.title: PDE engine swap, FV (VCell FV_SOLVER scheme) vs FEniCSx Q1 under the same coupling
investigations.objective:
Can the PDE half of the co-simulation be swapped for a different discretization
(FEniCSx, Q1 finite elements) without changing anything else, and does that change the
coupled result beyond discretization error?

investigations.name: field-modulated-decay
investigations.description:
The reaction is written once in the HybridModel (A + B -> B, k). partition() sends the
PDE side nothing (B is a catalyst), and sends the particle side A -> 0 with the rate
k*B; that Smoldyn evaluates through GridValueProvider at each molecule's nearest node.
Coupling is coupling: fvsolver with k = 1 (dt = 0.01).
investigations.title: Field-to-particle coupling, A_particle -> 0 at rate k·[B](x)
investigations.objective:
Does the Smoldyn process read the PDE field at each molecule as vcell-fvsolver does
(nearest node, value from the previous coupling step)? Does the coupled model approach
its deterministic continuum limit?

investigations.name: handoff-units-and-binning
investigations.description:
The FV operator is the one in vcell-fvsolver's FV_SOLVER (backward-Euler diffusion,
volume-scaled zero-flux Laplacian); tests/test_grid_and_fv.py checks its discrete
eigenmodes exactly. Here it is compared to the continuum solution. Particle runs use the
full process-bigraph composite (SmoldynHybrid with no fields), so the histogram handoff
is the production path.
investigations.title: Each side alone, and the particle-to-grid handoff
investigations.objective:
Before coupling anything: does each half of the co-simulation behave correctly on its own,
and does the particle-to-grid handoff (nearest-node binning, boundary element volumes,
counts to µM) follow vcell-fvsolver's conventions?

investigations.name: near-membrane-fields
investigations.description:
New helper: viva_pde_particle.reference.vcell_vtk.smoothed_domain builds pyvcell's smoothed
grid (from_mesh3d_volume → get_volume_vtk_grid → smooth_unstructured_grid_surface) from a
native .mesh file and maps node data onto its cells by global index.

Finding on the exporter: pyvcell and VCell's Java exporter (vis CartesianMesh.getVolumeElementBox)
draw element i as [i·L/N, (i+1)·L/N]. vcell-fvsolver's mesh is node-centred (node i at
i·L/(N−1)). On this 37³ mesh the exported cell domain is 8.4% smaller than the ball, and
elements are shifted by up to ~0.1 µm. smoothed_domain maps the corners onto node-centred
voxels before smoothing (node_centred=True). That is an analysis-side correction;
pyvcell itself is unchanged.

The mean native field on the smoothed grid is written to results/native_mean_B_smoothed.vtu
(open it in ParaView).
investigations.title: Fields next to a curved membrane: native VCell on pyvcell's smoothed grid vs co-sim on a body-fitted mesh
investigations.objective:
B2b found that the native hybrid loses molecules at the curved membrane. Where does that
show up in the field, and does the co-simulation have its own boundary artifact?
Native fields are read on pyvcell's smoothed unstructured grid, so boundary elements sit
near the true membrane rather than on the staircase.

investigations.name: performance-scaling
investigations.title: Wall time of the co-simulation vs the native VCell hybrid, with breakdown
investigations.objective:
What does decomposing the hybrid solver into process-bigraph processes cost? How does
the co-simulation's wall time compare with the native embedded solver as the grid and
the particle count grow, and how much of it is framework overhead?

investigations.name: sbml-spatial-hybrid
investigations.description:
Phase 6 (docs/PLAN.md). The representation annotation and its import/export are in VCell
(virtualcell/vcell#2175); libvcell adds `vcml_convert_units` (virtualcell/libvcell#26) and
pyvcell `load_sbml_str(..., unit_system="vcell")` (virtualcell/pyvcell#63; VCell imports SBML in the SBML's own units). Needs those builds:
`run.py` uses `run_native(..., sbml=...)` and `from_sbml`.

Found on the way: VCell's spatial stochastic math is only consistent in VCell's default
units. A hybrid imported in VCell's SBML units (dm, µmol, l) gave Smoldyn a world in dm with
creation rates per µm³, so field-driven creation produced almost nothing. VCell's SBML import
now converts such models to its default units.
investigations.title: The hybrid model described in SBML Spatial, run on both solvers
investigations.objective:
Can a PDE/particle hybrid be described in SBML Spatial, with each species' representation
(continuous or particle) as a VCell annotation, and run unchanged from that SBML on both
the native VCell solver and the co-simulation?

investigations.name: separable-calcium-sparks
investigations.description:
Channels are immobile particle species C (closed) and O (open), one per channel node.
Calcium U is a PDE field, and influx is a PDE source k·[O] with k = J·602.214.
- The native reference goes through VCell's own math generation (pyvcell → libvcell
  → vcell-fvsolver/Smoldyn 2.38), with two documented .smoldynInput post-processing
  steps (viva_pde_particle.reference.vcell_native):
  1. channels are placed at their nodes, because a BioModel cannot express per-node
     particle counts;
  2. VCell's no-op jump process O → O (from the influx) is dropped. In Smoldyn it would
     suppress channel closing (competing first-order reactions), which raises the open
     fraction from 1/6 to about 0.9.
- The reference E[U] is computed on the same grid with a fine step (dt_ref = 1e-4).

Deviations from the paper, both PROVISIONAL:
- Δz = 0.25 (3 z-nodes). Current VCell requires at least 3 nodes per axis; the paper
  used Δz = 0.5.
- Channel coordinates: the paper shows 4 columns of 6 (Fig 1A) without coordinates.
  Here, x = 2, 4, 6, 8 µm and y = 0.3 ... 1.8 µm on the z = 0 layer (approved by the
  author for now).
investigations.title: Schaff et al. 2016, Test 1 / Fig 1B: separable calcium sparks on both solvers
investigations.objective:
Do the native VCell hybrid solver and the process-bigraph co-simulation both reproduce
Fig 1B of Schaff et al. (2016)? The error of the trial-mean calcium against its exact
expectation should fall as N^-1/2 with the number of trials, and be statistically
dominated at small Δt.

investigations.name: single-channel-fokker-planck
investigations.description:
The references are in viva_pde_particle.benchmarks.fokker_planck:
- `fast_steady_state`: the closed form of Eq 4's stationary density,
  p ∝ (a − ρ)^(α−1) ρ^(αβ−1) e^(αβρ);
- `solve_fast`: upwind finite volumes, backward Euler;
- `solve_master`: Eq T2.1, explicit and matrix-free, with `extrapolate`.

The equations come from the paper and its S2 Text. The finite-diffusion model is `imax` equal cells
of width Δx with the channel in cell 0. The co-sim reproduces it with the new `element_volumes`
option of `build_hybrid_document`, which gives every node a full Δx in both the PDE and the
adapter (the node-centred grid would halve the end nodes).

**Deviations:**
- Test 5 runs at Δτ = 10⁻⁴, not 2 × 10⁻⁵.
- Tests 4–5 run only the co-simulation: VCell's node-centred mesh has half-volume end nodes, a
  different discrete model from Eq T2.1.
- Test 3's cube is [0, 1]³ instead of [−0.5, 0.5]³ (Smoldyn placement); this is equivalent.
investigations.title: Schaff et al. 2016, Tests 3–5 / Figs 4–6: a coupled single channel against direct Fokker–Planck solutions
investigations.objective:
With a single channel whose opening is coupled to calcium (rate αβ(ρ(0) + 1)), does the hybrid
co-simulation reproduce the probability densities of calcium given by direct, Monte-Carlo-free
solutions of the Fokker–Planck equations? Two regimes: fast diffusion (well mixed, Test 3) and
finite diffusion on coarse grids (Tests 4–5), as in Figs 4–6 of the paper.

investigations.name: sphere-cosim-vs-native
investigations.title: Same ball, two discretizations: native VCell (Cartesian + membrane numerics) vs co-simulation (body-fitted P1)
investigations.objective:
On a curved domain (a ball), how do the native VCell hybrid and the co-simulation compare?
- Native VCell uses analytic geometry on its Cartesian volume grid: the membrane is a
  staircase geometrically, but numerically uses local tangent-plane projections and
  Voronoi neighbours.
- The co-simulation uses a body-fitted P1 mesh coupled through a background grid.

investigations.name: splitting-schemes
investigations.description:
HybridCoupler composes the same FVReactionDiffusion and SmoldynHybrid engines and only
orders their substeps. Its jacobi scheme reproduces the two-process composite with
coupling="fvsolver" exactly (same seeds give identical counts; regression test in
tests/test_hybrid_cosim.py).
investigations.title: Operator-splitting schemes for PDE/particle coupling: Jacobi (fvsolver), Gauss–Seidel, Strang
investigations.objective:
The embedded vcell-fvsolver hard-codes one lagged (Jacobi-type) splitting. With the
coupling expressed as process-bigraph processes, can other splittings be used, and how
much accuracy do they buy at a given coupling interval?

investigations.name: two-way-exchange
investigations.description:
This study found two defects in Smoldyn's grid-based 0th-order creation (the
OPTION_VCELL path), both now fixed in our fork (virtualcell/Smoldyn pyhybrid):
1. **Full-cell volume:** the count used the full cell volume at boundary nodes, as in
   vcell-fvsolver's embedded Smoldyn 2.38 (reported as virtualcell/vcell-fvsolver#24).
2. **Skipped boundary nodes:** nodes on the domain walls failed the geometric
   compartment test, so boundary cells never produced. VCell's voxel-map compartments
   avoid this.
A remaining Smoldyn start-up artifact skips creation for about the first 2 steps
(about 1% over 2 s).
The native solver still has defect 1, so it does not conserve mass here. This study
quantifies the native bias rather than masking it.
investigations.title: Mass balance across the particle ↔ field handoff
investigations.objective:
When molecules move both ways between particle and field representations (A_particle
→ B_field and B_field → A_particle by field-dependent creation), is total A + B
conserved and is the right steady state reached? Do both solvers agree?

investigations.name: unstructured-geometry
investigations.title: Hybrid co-simulation with a body-fitted unstructured PDE mesh (ball)
investigations.objective:
Can the co-simulation use a body-fitted unstructured mesh for the PDE half of a curved
domain, as an alternative to VCell's own Cartesian volume grid with staircase-membrane
numerics, while keeping the particle ↔ field handoff conservative and accurate?

investigations.name: vcell-geometry-cosim
investigations.description:
Infrastructure (Phase 7e.5):
- `geometry/accessible.py`: accessible fractions, the fold map and effective volumes for the
  three variants;
- `GridCountsToConcentration` with a `staircase` option (fold and volumes), and the new
  `ExtendGridField` Step;
- an FV `domain` option (mask and volume fractions) with a masked diffusion matrix;
- `build_vcell_geometry_hybrid_document`.

Found while building it: VTK's `vtkSelectEnclosedPoints` misclassifies lattice-aligned points
against VCell's smooth surface, depending on process state (inside fraction 0.16 against a true
0.33 after a composite had been created). The VCell realization now uses a robust vertical-ray
parity test (`geometry/inside.py`). The B2c forward model's lattice results were re-checked
with it and are unchanged (96 staircase nodes outside the smooth membrane).
investigations.title: The co-simulation on VCell's own geometry: staircase PDE, smooth membrane, accessible-volume correction
investigations.objective:
Native VCell solves the PDE on the voxel staircase but confines particles by a smooth membrane.
For the B2b ball the two domains differ by ~1.8% in volume. That leaves a −1.4% outer-shell
depletion and an exchange drift, even with the binning correction of vcell-fvsolver#25
(Study B2c). With the co-simulation running on exactly VCell's geometry, can an
accessible-volume correction make the coupling both unbiased and conservative?
